title: Lomo Saltado

qty.note: about 1.5 lb, cut into 2-inch strips against the grain
split between the potatoes and the wok

steps.text: Start the rice: rinse it, then cook with 1 1/2 cups water, covered, over the lowest heat for 15 minutes. Keep the lid on while you work; it steams in its own heat.
Pat the beef strips dry and season them with half the salt and all the black pepper. Dry beef sears; wet beef steams.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wide skillet over medium-high. Lay the potatoes in one layer and fry for 12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until tender inside with deep gold edges. Drain on a plate.

Wipe the skillet, add the last tbsp of oil, and raise the heat to high. When the oil shimmers, add the beef in one uncrowded layer. Sear 2 minutes, turning once. Beef strips are safe at 145°F (63°C) — spot-check the thickest strip on a thermometer.

safety.source: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperature table

steps.text: Push the beef to the edge of the pan. Add the onion wedges and stir-fry 1 minute — they should stay crisp, barely losing their bite.
Add the garlic for 15 seconds, then the tomato wedges, and toss twice. Saltado means 'jumped': the point is a quick toss, not a stew.
Pour the soy sauce and lime juice down the side of the pan, return the fries, and toss everything 30 seconds so the sauce coats and the fries stay crisp.
Fluff the rice. Plate the saltado over rice with the pan juices poured on top, and scatter the cilantro over all of it.

cuisine_note: Lomo saltado is Peru's Chinese-Peruvian (chifa) bistro dish: hot pan, soy and lime, and potatoes stir-fried right in with the beef instead of served beside it.
